previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, diabetes, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for evaluation of melena present for four days, associated with occasional lightheadedness and right upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the back. Initial workup revealed guaiac-positive stools but a negative nasogastric lavage. An ultrasound showed cholelithiasis without cholecystitis. During the emergency department stay, he developed transient substernal chest pain typical of angina, which resolved with sublingual nitroglycerin and morphine; cardiac enzymes were negative. He underwent an upper endoscopy that revealed erosive gastritis without active bleeding. He was started on intravenous pantoprazole and discharged on oral esomeprazole 40 mg twice daily. An H. pylori antibody test was negative. A capsule endoscopy was scheduled for outpatient follow-up. His cardiac and renal medications were continued without change, and he was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to return for any recurrent bleeding, chest pain, or other concerning symptoms.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ man with chest pain, abdominal pain.  Rule out aneurysm.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis on ___ and CTA chest on ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were acquired from the thoracic inlet to the pubic
symphysis without iv contrast.  Multiplanar reformatted images were obtained
for evaluation. IV contrast not given due to impending cardiac catheterization
and per request from primary team.

CT CHEST WITHOUT IV CONTRAST: The right chest eall dual-lead cardiac pacemaker
is again seen with the leads terminating in the right atrium and ventricle.
Moderate cardiomegaly is again noted. There is no pericardial effusion.
Significant coronary artery calcifications are again noted.  There is evidence
of prior CABG.  Significant calcification noted along the aorta, though there
is aneurysm or intramural hematoma. The airway is centrally patent.

There is right sided pleural thickening with more nodular thickening noted
along the posterior RUL, RLL, as well and the RML. There is small right
basilar pleural effusion with right lower lobe nodular consolidation appearing
similar to CT from ___.  A small focal consolidation is again noted
in the lateral aspect of the right middle lobe, similar in appearance.
Prominent extrapleural fat is noted on the right, likely secondary to chronic
pleural disease. There is no pneumothorax.

CT ABDOMEN WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:  The noncontrast appearance of the liver,
spleen, pancreas and adrenals is normal. There is hyperattenuating material in
the dependent portion of the gallbladder, compatible with the known
cholelithiasis.  There is no pericholestatic fluid or any secondary signs of
acute cholecystitis.  Extensive vascular calcification noted. The kidneys are
within normal limits. There is no hydronephrosis or hydroureter.  The stomach,
duodenum and loops of small bowel are normal. There is no free fluid or free
air in the intra- abdominal cavity. No gross lymphadenopathy is noted. Mild
gynecomastia is noted.

CT PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST:  The appendix is normal. The colon is normal with
fecal matter and bowel gas.  The bladder is only minimally distended but no
gross abnormality is noted.  Again noted is moderate-to-severe vascular
calcification along the aorta and its major branches.  The endovascular stent
in the distal aortic and bilateral iliac arteries is noted without gross
abnormality.  There is no free air or fluid in the pelvis.  No gross
lymphadenopathy is seen.

BONE WINDOW:  Again noted is mild-to-moderate degenerative disease, most
evident in the lower lumbar.  There is no acute fracture or dislocation.  No
worrisome lytic or sclerotic osseous lesion is seen.

IMPRESSION: 
1.  Stable right lung consolidation with pleural thickening, small right
pleural effusion.
2.  Cholelithiasis without acute cholecystitis.  
3.  Atherosclerotic disease.
4.  Cardiomegaly.

REASON FOR EXAM:  Right upper quadrant pain.  Clinical concern for
cholecystitis.

COMPARISON:  CT from ___.  Abdominal ultrasound from ___.

ULTRASOUND IMAGES OF THE RUQ:  The liver shows no textural or focal
abnormalities.  The gallbladder contains gallstones and sludge.  There is a
0.5 cm gallbladder polyp, stable. There is no GB wall edema or
___ fluid. Common duct is not dilated.  The pancreas is obscured
by overlying bowel gas.

IMPRESSION:
1. Cholelithiasis with no definite evidence of cholecystitis.
2. Stable 0.5 cm gallbladder polyp.
